note: Rabbi Shimon told how, in the village of Pani, an old man asked him whether Rabbi Akiva really said that sprinkling the blood takes effect for sacrificial meat that has left the courtyard, and he answered yes. His colleagues in the Galilee objected: the meat is unfit, so how can the sprinkling work for it? When he brought this to Rabbi Akiva, Akiva said: my son, don't you agree? He pointed to two sin offerings, a lost one and its replacement, where sprinkling the blood of one frees the other's meat from the laws of misuse even though that other animal is unfit; all the more should the blood free its own meat.
why: Rabbi Akiva's comparison was cited and then limited by Rabbi Elazar to two animals slaughtered at once; right after this account, Reish Lakish says Akiva gave his student a misleading answer.
